editorial.description: After Val Kilmer's death, Choe uses an object found by his son and a hummingbird drawing to remember Kilmer's physical presence, voice after throat illness and layered screen identities, while reflecting on details that become visible only after loss.
editorial.summary: After Val Kilmer's death, Choe uses an object found by his son and a hummingbird drawing to remember Kilmer's physical presence, voice after throat illness and layered screen identities, while reflecting on details that become visible only after loss. This is an official-channel creative lesson or reflection, not clinical treatment or a universal formula. Its chronological map follows the route's own transcript and distinguishes art-making instructions from autobiographical claims, jokes and metaphors. Visually dependent technique still requires the source video.
